To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) for homogeneous soil profiles, cumulative out-flow and profile-aver-aged soil water content data contained sufficient system information to estimate the soil hydraulic properties and the root distribution parameters simultaneously, (ii) for soil profiles consisting in two layers, the unique identification of the soil hydraulic properties was only possible if matric potential data from both layers were used in the objective function, and (iii) the system behavior under various boundary conditions can be predicted adequately with parameters that were estimated from actual data.

the soil hydraulic parameters of a lysimeter can be estimated from cumulative outflow and soil water content data, and that the rooting depth can be identified from the cumulative outflow and the profile-averaged data.
